title: Monarchy
objective: After this level you can explain how monarchies work.
summary: Monarchy means rule of one: a monarch who is head of state, usually by inheritance. Malaysia elects its ruler; Louis XIV claimed absolute power by divine right.

cards.headline: Malaysia's king changes every five years. His fellow rulers elect him.
cards.body: Malaysia's head of state, officially the paramount ruler, is elected from among nine hereditary state rulers for a five-year term. That makes him unusual. In most monarchies, nobody votes for the monarch at all. So what makes a monarchy a monarchy?

cards.headline: Rule of one
cards.body: The name gives it away. Monarchy comes from the Greek monarkhia, literally "ruling of one". Britannica defines it as a system based on the undivided rule of a single person. That person, the monarch, is head of state and usually gets the job by heredity. You don't apply for a throne. You're born next in line for it.

cards.headline: Why people went along with it
cards.body: Remember Weber's three roots of authority from Level 3? A monarch who inherits the throne was his example of traditional authority: power accepted because things have always been done this way. Many monarchs had something extra on their side. Britannica notes that successful and popular monarchs were believed to have a sacred right to rule.

cards.fact: Louis XIV of France is the textbook absolute monarch.
cards.context: Absolutism means unlimited, centralized authority, held especially by a monarch. Louis XIV, who reigned from 1643 to 1715, is Britannica's most familiar example. Its favorite defense was the divine right of kings: kings got their authority from God, so they answered to no one on Earth. That's more than seven decades of answering to no one.

cards.headline: Monarchy: crowned
learned: Monarchy means rule of one, usually by inheritance
Malaysia elects its ruler for five years
Inherited thrones rest on traditional authority
Louis XIV ruled as an absolute monarch by divine right

questions.prompt: Monarchy: the Greek word monarkhia literally means what?

options.label: Ruling of the many
options.rationale: That would be closer to democracy.

options.label: Ruling by the rich
options.rationale: Rule by the wealthy is a different word, and a later level.

options.label: Ruling by God
options.rationale: That's theocracy, coming up in Level 15.

questions.explanation: Monarchy comes from the Greek monarkhia, "ruling of one", from monos (alone) and arkhein (to rule).

questions.prompt: Why is Malaysia's paramount ruler unusual among monarchs?

options.label: He is elected for five years instead of inheriting the throne
He holds absolute power by divine right
options.rationale: Nothing in the level says so; what stands out is how he's chosen.

options.label: He is chosen by a vote of all Malaysian citizens
options.rationale: Only the nine hereditary state rulers elect him.

options.label: He shares the throne with a second king
options.rationale: There is one paramount ruler at a time.

questions.explanation: Most monarchs inherit the throne for life. Malaysia's is elected from among nine hereditary rulers for a five-year term.

questions.prompt: Absolute monarchy: Hobbes (Level 7) and the divine right of kings both backed an all-powerful ruler. Where did each say that power came from?

options.label: Both said it came from God
options.rationale: Hobbes grounded the sovereign's power in people's agreement, not God.

options.label: Hobbes: people handing over their freedom; divine right: God
Hobbes: God; divine right: an agreement among people
Both said it came from winning a war

questions.explanation: Hobbes had people hand their freedom to a sovereign in exchange for peace. The divine right of kings said kings got their authority from God.
